=== WHAT THIS PR DOES, AND THE ONE QUESTION THAT ACTUALLY MATTERS ===
It flips lwb-proof-reexecute from continue-on-error: true to false -- making it BLOCKING -- and adds a structural guard against a specific recording mistake. For a gate being armed, only one question really matters: DOES IT PASS, AND DOES IT PASS FOR THE RIGHT REASON? Both checked.

1. IT PASSES. `python scripts/lwb_check_proof.py --reexecute` on this branch: "TOTAL: 33 of 167 commands re-executed, 0 uncomparable, 19 skipped-self, across 24 records -- ALL RE-EXECUTED COMMANDS MATCHED", exit 0. So arming it does not turn its own PR red.

2. IT PASSES FOR THE RIGHT REASON, not because nothing was checked. This is the repository's signature defect pattern -- "I could not check" sharing a representation with "I checked and found nothing" -- and arming a gate is exactly when it becomes dangerous, because a vacuous pass now carries authority. It is genuinely closed here: `--reexecute` has a FOUR-WAY exit contract, and REEXECUTE_EXIT_NOTHING_REEXECUTED is 2, DISTINCT from REEXECUTE_EXIT_ALL_MATCHED (0), with REEXECUTE_EXIT_MISMATCH (1) and REEXECUTE_EXIT_UNCOMPARABLE (3) also separate. So a record set that exempts every command does NOT produce a green blocking gate -- it exits 2 and fails the job. The code says so in its own comment ("'nothing was re-executed' is never" conflated) and the tests cover it (tests/test_lwb_check_proof_reexecute.py asserts REEXECUTE_EXIT_NOTHING_REEXECUTED at four separate call sites, including a direct `rc == REEXECUTE_EXIT_NOTHING_REEXECUTED`). 33 of 167 were actually re-executed here, so this run is not the vacuous case anyway.

=== THE STRUCTURAL GUARD, MUTATION-PROBED ===
The PR adds STATE_DEPENDENT_COMMAND_NEEDLES ("lwb_handoff", "lwb_check_state_claims") and forbids `verifiable: true` on any command naming them, because their output embeds live repo STATE (HANDOFF.md's generated-block byte count; a scan of every tracked .md file's volatile git/PR claims) rather than tracked file CONTENT. The motivation is real and I verified it independently while reviewing #63: proof/39.json's recorded digest encodes "HANDOFF.md passes all checks (2961 bytes)", and `--reexecute` FAILS on untouched origin/main because main's HANDOFF.md is 2960 bytes. So this is a defect that exists on main right now, that this PR both fixes (proof/39.json) and prevents recurring (the guard). The docstring's claim that the identical mistake was made twice -- proof/20.json then proof/39.json, same command -- is consistent with everything I could see.

=== THE RESIDUAL WEAKNESS THE PR DISCLOSES ITSELF, WHICH I CONFIRMED AND WANT ON THE RECORD ===
The CI comment states plainly that the verifiable_reason enum constrains the WORDING of an opt-out, not whether the stated reason is TRUE, so "a record can still mark every command verifiable: false with a plausible reason and get a green gate having re-executed nothing -- ... visibility is not prevention. That judgement stays with review, not this script." That is honest and I confirmed the mechanism (exit 2 makes the all-exempt case fail, but a MOSTLY-exempt record passes on whatever remains).
I can sharpen it with something measured on the neighbouring PR: scripts/lwb_sanitise.py normalises absolute paths ONLY -- it has no timing normalisation -- so NO pytest invocation can ever be `verifiable: true`, because its output embeds an elapsed time. Every test-suite run in every proof record is therefore structurally exempt from the gate this PR is arming. The gate is about to become blocking over the 33 commands it can check while permanently unable to re-verify the single most important claim any deliverable makes: that its tests pass. That is NOT a defect of this PR -- it is a sanitiser limitation on main, and this PR neither causes it nor claims otherwise -- but "lwb-proof-reexecute is blocking" will read, to anyone who has not read this far, as a much stronger guarantee than it is. Worth a line in proof/README.md or the plan document. NOT BLOCKING.

VERDICT: AGREE. Arming this gate is justified and the arming is done carefully. The gate passes on its own branch and, critically, passes for the right reason: the four-way exit contract makes "nothing was re-executed" exit 2 rather than masquerade as success, which is precisely the failure mode that would make a blocking gate worse than a report-only one. The new structural guard closes a mistake this repo has demonstrably made twice on the same command, and mutation probes confirm every needle is covered by name in both the validator and the recorder. The ordering trap is clean despite the reviewable head being a merge that hand-resolved the HANDOFF.md conflict, commit identity is clean throughout including the merge, and the previously-won distinction between bounding a failure and bounding a hang survived the rewrite. I found no defect attributable to this PR. My one reservation is not a defect but a scope caveat worth stating loudly: the cross-platform digest reproduction that justifies arming this gate is historical evidence I could not re-verify from Linux, and this PR's own six-legged CI matrix is where it must be confirmed before merge.
